relevance_note: A three-generation family in which a heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant was found and 'P1–P7 were all diagnosed with HA20', each described individually.
method_note: Read the whole paper manually and built the JSON with a short Python script that only encodes my reading; no table was transcribed by script. Tables 1 and 2 and Figs. 1 and 2 have captions only in the Markdown (no cell content), so thyroid test values, antibody titres, HLA types and the pedigree are unavailable; the family has no printed family label. Seven family members P1–P7 are individuals; the c.2209delC variant is attributed to all seven from 'analyzed TNFAIP3 in the present family (P1–P7)' + 'present in all members tested' + 'Hence, P1–P7 were all diagnosed with HA20' (the Case Presentation says only 'present in all the HT members tested', so whether every one of P1–P7 was genotyped is not fully explicit). Four previously published HA20 patients described individually in the Discussion were added under label rule 4 (ref (2) patient, ref (2) patient 2, ref (4) patient, ref (15) patient); they get no variant rows because the paper only calls them 'HA20 patient' and prints no variant; ref (2) is the Japanese HA20 cohort that also included this family, so overlap of 'ref (2) patient 2' (GD case) with this family cannot be excluded from the text, although no family member is described with GD. HLA alleles/haplotype (A*24:02-B*54:01-C*01:02-DRB1*14:03 in P2–P5; HLA-B27 in ref (2) patient) are risk alleles and were not recorded as variants. Inheritance was not inferred per person although the paper calls the trait autosomal dominant; only P1's parental testing statement is filled (mother P2 is a tested carrier). Ethnicity 'Japanese' for P1–P7 comes from the statement that this family was part of Kadowaki et al.'s study of 'nine independent Japanese families'. Ages of HT diagnosis (P2 28 yr, P3 27 yr; P5 findings at 9 yr; P4 at craniopharyngioma diagnosis) are recorded as feature detail, not as age_at_diagnosis, because the disease label is HA20 and its diagnosis age is not given. Current ages 'currently 6-, 2-, and 1-yr-old, respectively' were split to P1, P6, P7 (shared unit distributed). P1, P6 and P7: 'normal thyroid functions and no anti-thyroid autoantibodies' recorded as excluded features and autoimmune thyroiditis checklist = excluded, despite the authors' caveat that they 'are too young for this to be apparent'. Stomatitis (P3, P4) was not mapped to the checklist item 'oral ulcers' because ulcers are not stated; P2's 'possible Crohn's disease' and P7's perineal fistula 'possibly associated with inflammatory bowel disease' were not mapped to GI inflammation; P4's Hodgkin lymphoma and craniopharyngioma were not mapped to lymphoproliferation or CNS involvement. Contradiction: the variant is called 'novel' in the abstract and results, but the Discussion says its in vitro functional analysis 'was previously reported' (ref 2) and the family was previously described in ref 2.
